Michael, trading is not a complex business, traders make it complicated for themselves. And the question you ask is very difficult to answer so that it is understandable. Getting words to fit what I look for is not a formula or science. It is looking back through history where professional money was active, and why they were active there. This means starting from high time frames and working down to the time frame you feel most comfortable with and can afford.

There are principles that apply to all currencies and indices more than stocks. Stocks in my view are manipulated due to the volume of the stock and other shall we say knowledge, and leave it at that.

The principles are:

Support Resistance Demand (buyers) Supply (sellers) Decision areas Price action

Then the lesser areas of importance such as round numbers and price patterns. Price doesnt make a pattern, humans make a pattern out of it. And round numbers are just on the way to the next number, but used to good effect by the media etc.

Support which forms with demand is good. Resistance which forms with supply is good.

Both when formed on higher time frames where all the lower time frames have had their opportunity to cycle or phase through, is really good. Decision areas when formed at historic areas where price stalled are good, but traded only after some time in the market i.e screen time. king of all is price action, this is where pro money can no longer hide their orders and the market reacts to the heave of orders.

Most people will get the principles of support/resistance, demand/buyers, decision areas, but most will fail on price action. There is no short cut to reading price action because you must learn to read it on the fly and as it unfolds live. When price action happens with any of the above principles you must be ready to act. What will throw most traders is they are trading counter intuitive to the markets direction. If the trade was so easy to see there would in effect be no trade to take because the flood of orders would make the move happen to quickly. Real trades behave to what the herd calls trending. Trends are pro money at work and it wont stop until their target is hit, and then they mostly try and create a false impression at the end of their move of it continuing forever and the herd responds as they do with an easy way for pro money to trade against and take their vast profits.

Charts posted of trades will help you more than any book or course ever can. I am not surprised that the past month has been difficult for you, I took off a month in December for the same reason you were confused, I know the markets get choppy at years end and start of the next, so there is no reason to trade. In fact there was only the last two weeks of February where there was good trades. The drift down we had is not worth taking and we are now in a range. Dont expect the charts to make sense when you see such choppy conditions. Wait for them to recover and give direction, then wait for an entry when an obvious target is hit and be on the side of pro money always, it is after all where the real money is.

Have you seen the videos made by IF (hippy guy with long hair and magic mushrooms behind his ear) they are worth watching. They will help get a feel for a market as he steps through the moves.

Although similar to s/r it differs in respect to the power of the move which in this case showed that the bears were firmly in control.j The desire to sell here was overwhelming. I waited longer than usual so that I could see how the pro's were going to unwind their long positions and not cause too much of a rapid decline. The reversal was rather hard and sudden and there is a lot of money going south at the moment and no target for some distance below.

A few charts to help aid you. The 4hr zoomed out first.

You can see how price climbed painfully back into old demand and there was no sign of pro money there, and if no buyers came in when that area was reached it was a given that price will either consolidate or fall. The out come as you know now was a dramatic fall. It shoild not come of much a surprise given the sell offs further up, but the old demand area put up a fight for a few days. Seeing price come back up underneath us next should also be no surprise, unless the bears really want to push hard into their target which on the large time frame is a nice long run.

A closer look this time with the 30min chart.

Note on the bottom of the chart there is a weak buying area and this too shows little pro money coming in for longs, there is no follow through. As price heads back to resistance note the last major bullish candle and a later change in bias with price setting up a nice S/R area and it was only in that price action area where we could see some clarity and intent of pro money. it is clear we had a concerted effort to push price hard into the old demand area and it stalled only for a little while before breaking through. Only at this point was I willing to sell.

Finally a 1min chart for some entries and you wont often see me post these low time frames, its very hard to tell where anyone got an entry off a 1min chart, but if you look for the places where price went back up into supply and the broker spread, you will see my entries. I have many overlayed entries on this chart and all are within a tidy and relatively small support/resistance price range and where there is clear bearish bias in the market. For those who are not scalpers or break out traders you have already much information in this site on what to do.

When the market breaks out you wait for a pull back to the origin of the move or at least into the origin area i.e within the full extension of the candles near the origin. This revisit is pro money looking to either add more positions or have the break out appear as a false break trapping those who are trigger happy.

What you risk in the search for profit determines what kind of trader you are. Speaking for myself I will only trade off areas where it is clear pro money is active and the direction also clear.

At the moment we have had a break, now I wait for a retest of the origin, then price action. To my eyes, if the move is not a continuation move down I will not take a bullish entry no matter how good it looks.

Where you pull the trigger and in what direction is your call alone Castus.

It serves multiple purposes. Take out stops, fill orders in the opposite direction, increase momentum and give the impression the move is reversing. Pro money will trade against itself, for a time. It is necessary to help filter in more orders.

Taking a position in a pull back is counter intuitive to most traders and the thoughts of scaling with orders in the opposite direction to price movement is hard for them to do. It is not logical in their minds.

چند هدف دارد. گرفتن استاپ‌ها، پرکردن سفارش‌ها در جهت مخالف، افزایش مومنتوم و دادن این تصور که حرکت دارد برمی‌گردد. پول حرفه‌ای برای مدتی خلاف خودش معامله می‌کند. برای کمک به فیلترکردن سفارش‌های بیشتر ضروری است.

Hi Blacky,

There is a mind set out there that sees all candle with long tails and wicks as reasons to place an entry. These are not always entries and unless they happen at longer time frames I rarely take them. The exceptions are for day trading where I look at lower time frames for a continuation move after a pull back from the higher time/missed entry took place. But what is common and always must be shown is taking it with support/demand for buying, or resistance/supply for selling.

At present we are just into a new month, I wonder how many people here have looked at the monthly closed candle this week?....it is easy to forget this.

Your loosing trade should be very obvious why it is loosing. Look on your 4hr chart, you went long off a 30min pull back and expected that to hold. The 4hr time frame has much more weight over a 30min chart and given price was also just finished with hitting resistance you were standing in the way of a raging bear. Not a good place to be. If you drew your 4hr upper blue line higher and where real supply came in historically you would have been getting better intel. It is apparent that the line was the cause of your wrong entry and the 30min chart where you saw support was pre mature. If you can, allow at least the 4hr chart to unwind before placing a trade, it will be safer and have more weight in the direction of price. Then drop down to your 30min, 15min etc and get a finer view on price action and take an entry on a pull back on that lower time frame where you see price ending the counter trend move.

I am aware that this is not always easy to do and teaching your brain to accept price must rise before pro money shorts it, and price must fall before pro money takes it long is not logical.....yet!

These pull backs are where I enter most times, and it is rather boring in fact because it is the same trick played over and over and dressed up with a different candle formation. But price, actual price, cannot be hidden in their games because we know there are narrow bands of price where a move must take place in order for targets be met. If this makes no sense now, it will in time.

Hope this helps you Blacky, feel free to post any time you wish here and I will help where I can.

در حال حاضر تازه وارد ماه جدید شده‌ایم؛ کنجکاوم چند نفر اینجا چارت ماهانهٔ بسته‌شدهٔ این هفته را نگاه کرده‌اند؟… فراموش‌کردن این آسان است.

معامله بازنده‌ات باید خیلی واضح باشد چرا بازنده است. روی چارت 4hr‌ت نگاه کن؛ از روی پولبک 30min خرید شدی و انتظار داشتی نگه دارد. تایم‌فریم 4hr وزن بسیار بیشتری نسبت به چارت 30min دارد و با توجه به اینکه قیمت همین حالا تازه به مقاومت خورده بود، تو جلوی یک خرسِ خشمگین ایستاده بودی. جای خوبی نبود. اگر خط آبی بالای 4hr را بالاتر و جایی که عرضهٔ واقعی در تاریخچه وارد شده بود می‌کشیدی، اطلاعات بهتری می‌گرفتی. آشکار است خط علت ورود غلط تو بود و چارت 30min که در آن حمایت دیدی زودرس بود. اگر می‌توانی، حداقل بگذار چارت 4hr قبل از گذاشتن معامله کارش را تمام کند؛ امن‌تر خواهد بود و وزن بیشتری در جهت قیمت دارد. بعد به 30min، 15min و غیره برو و دید ظریف‌تری از price action بگیر و روی پولبکی در آن تایم‌فریم پایین‌تر جایی که می‌بینی حرکت خلاف روند دارد تمام می‌شود ورود بگیر.

می‌دانم این همیشه آسان نیست و آموختن به مغزت که بپذیرد قیمت باید قبل از اینکه پول حرفه‌ای آن را فروش کند بالا برود و قبل از خرید‌شدن باید پایین برود منطقی نیست… هنوز!

این پولبک‌ها جایی‌اند که بیشتر وقت‌ها وارد می‌شوم و در واقع کاملاً خسته‌کننده است چون همان ترفند بارها و بارها تکرار می‌شود و با فرم کندلی متفاوت آراسته می‌شود. اما قیمت، قیمت واقعی، در بازی‌هایشان پنهان نمی‌شود چون می‌دانیم نوارهای باریکی از قیمت هست که حرکت باید در آن‌ها اتفاق بیفتد تا تارگت‌ها خورده شوند. اگر الان این به ذهنت معنا نمی‌دهد، به‌تدریج می‌دهد.

Doctor wrote: Some light candle reading for you all. The pun's come early on today.

First chart is monthly chart, the pair involved is meaningless and I removed as much from the chart to concentrate your eye and brain.

Look at where price is now and can you determine the reason for the current candle, and lets assume it is a closed candle.

Here is the same chart with a little detail, and just enough to show whats going on. We again assume a closed candle and we see a reaction of support and old demand, the price goes up. The likely target?....the box above. All simple, no fuss and nothing difficult to understand.

Lets really get into the details now.

Here is a zoomed in view of the last leg down in price. To help guide your eye here, candle 1 was a race to grab old demand and is also taken at support.

2 the bulls have already got their work done and the follow through buy intraday bears is weak the close well off the lows.

3 the bulls intent is obvious here with a very large body and close with very little wick on top. On the other chart you will see this candle hit old supply.

4 considering we just hit old supply this candle close showed such weak bullish momentum that it was plain to see we need to fall back down, or collect more orders to break above.

5 a weak bearish candle, note how it closed well inside the previous candles low, note the long tail, a sign of buying.

6 a very strong bull candle with strong close above support, so we long this puppy to the moon now right?

7 no, we wait for a pull back and see does support hold. And 7 is a perfect bearish engulfing candle and proves candle 6 was a false bullish break.

8 unfortunately the market timing for the previous move was not very good and we are now stuck between close in old supply and demand. When this happens we need to keep the big picture in mind, we are still below supply. This candle attempts to grab more orders from the bulls by the tail showing buying, however the weak close tells is its going nowhere.

9 we have a break below near term candle 5 and old demand from candle 3. But hitting candle 3's demand hard means we have to see a reaction higher.

10 this is the reaction from candle 9, it has setup up pro money for the main bearish move.

11 this is interesting, the candle pushed lower than the previous candles wick and closed within the body of candle 3 which is still the most significant candle we need to break.

12 finally a strong break and strong close. Of note here is the candle got into the tail of candle 1. There were a lot of buyers here and even though it is not the first time price has been in that area, there is validity given to this area given its likely hood to act as resistance once broken and retested.

13 no interest in taking price lower yet and no progress made by bulls or bears. The very slight tail below the tiny body means we wait.

14 this is the start of the pro bears selling. See how the wick pulls in supply from candle 12 and closes as a bullish looking candle but with a very low close on the candle 12 body. Books will tell you this is a bullish engulfing candle because it had contained the previous candle, correct, but, the books fail to tell you the reason for the wick and where it went.

15 Something to look at on this candle is the fact that the body is both bearish and closed within the previous candle, but no takers higher considering candle 14 is what is considered bullish. Pro money know better.

16 This is the bug push to get the market running and all the work prior to this candle was done in candle 14 and a lot of bears waited for this move whereas candle 14 would have got day traders long and now candle 16 would have stopped them out adding fuel to the bearish orders. Also note candles 12, 13, 14, 15 are all at S/R.

17 not much to say, we are moving down at a nice clip and money being made by the bears, dont stand in front of this freight train, be on it.

18 The line at the bottom of my chart is old demand taken from the chart earlier up. So why has price suddenly stopped and gone bullish?....two reasons, not all pro money has the same take profit target and some will bail before the ultimate target. This candle shows profit taking, which in itself has pinned the last of the bears who entered at the close of 16 which is 17's open. Who would have guessed it setup one final small move down. But on this time frame is enough to buy a nice lunch:)

19 old demand pinned to the pixel and also the first sign of the market slowing down. The tail tells us this. When the market is running hard it will not stop on a dime and the tails and wicks you see at major old price level on higher time frames has to be traded against in the opposite direction by pro money to first stop the current move and setup the next. This is never a cheap exercise and costs a lot of money. We see the wicks and tails and look for our entries.

20. Given pro money reached their target it was of no surprise we will at least see one small leg up and possibly a retest of the newly created low.

21 so far we are no longer bearish and now bullish, but a retest of the low is still on the cards unless we see a test of new support coming along and this may look like a decision point. Possible places for a sensible decision are candle 18, 13 thru 15 cluster.

The time frame for this doesnt matter because price which is plotted in time is a fractal of itself and keeping all the old support and demand areas from higher time frames for use on lower time frame charts is essential for success. An example would be a 1 or 5 min trader taking a short at candle 19 because it was a break of 18, but not understanding that he was shorting into a major higher time frame of buyers.

The other horizontal lines on the chart are a partial guide to help train your eye and logical side of your brain. There are more places to find support and resistance and I will let you look for those.

If you are willing to wait price will always show you a clear direction and when its turned. There are times when even a 5min trade wont come around for a day or so. This chart is primarily for a trader in the US who made a nice gesture to me and I am returning both his appreciation and letting him know there is more value in money alone. Everyone else has some more material to study, so thank our US friend for coming up with this idea of a numbered candle stick chart.

Have a good weekend everyone.

Doctor نوشت: کمی کندل‌خوانی سبک برای همهٔ شما. بازی کلامی‌ها امروز زود آمده‌اند.

اولین چارت، چارت ماهانه است؛ جفت درگیر بی‌معنی است و تا جای ممکن از چارت حذف کردم تا چشمت و ذهنت را متمرکز کنم.

به جایی که قیمت الان است نگاه کن؛ می‌توانی دلیل کندل فعلی را تشخیص بدهی؟ و فرض کنیم کندل بسته‌شده است.

این همان چارت با کمی جزئیات است، و به‌اندازهٔ کافی تا نشان دهد چه دارد می‌گذرد. باز هم کندل بسته‌شده فرض می‌کنیم و واکنشی از حمایت و تقاضای قدیمی می‌بینیم؛ قیمت بالا می‌رود. تارگت محتمل؟… باکس بالایی. همه‌چیز ساده است، بدون سر و صدا و هیچ چیز سخت برای فهمیدن نیست.

حالا واقعاً وارد جزئیات شویم.

این دید بزرگ‌شدهٔ آخرین leg نزولی قیمت است. برای راهنمایی چشمت اینجا، کندل 1 مسابقه‌ای برای گرفتن تقاضای قدیمی بود و روی حمایت هم گرفته شده است.

2 صعودی‌ها کارشان را از قبل کرده‌اند و خریدِ ادامه‌دهنده توسط خرس‌های intraday ضعیف است؛ کندل خوب بالای کف‌ها بسته شده.

3 قصد صعودی‌ها اینجا با بدنهٔ بسیار بزرگ و بسته‌شدن با سایهٔ خیلی کم در بالا آشکار است. در چارت دیگر می‌بینی این کندل به عرضهٔ قدیمی خورده است.

4 با توجه به اینکه همین حالا به عرضهٔ قدیمی خوردیم، این بسته‌شدن کندل مومنتوم صعودی ضعیفی نشان داد که به‌وضوح می‌شد ببینیم باید دوباره پایین برویم یا سفارش‌های بیشتری جمع کنیم تا بالای آن بشکنیم.

5 کندل نزولی ضعیف؛ توجه کن چطور خوب داخل کف کندل قبلی بسته شد، به دم بلند توجه کن، نشانهٔ خرید.

6 کندل صعودی بسیار قوی با بستن قوی بالای حمایت؛ پس این توله‌سگ را خرید می‌کنیم تا ماه، درسته؟

7 نه، منتظر پولبک می‌مانیم و می‌بینیم آیا حمایت نگه می‌دارد. و 7 کندل اینگالف نزولی کاملی است و ثابت می‌کند کندل 6 یک شکست صعودی فیک بوده است.

8 متأسفانه زمان‌بندی بازار برای حرکت قبلی خیلی خوب نبود و الان بین عرضه و تقاضای قدیمیِ نزدیک گیر کرده‌ایم. وقتی این اتفاق می‌افتد باید تصویر بزرگ را در ذهن نگه داریم؛ هنوز زیر عرضه هستیم. این کندل با دمش که خرید را نشان می‌دهد سعی می‌کند سفارش‌های بیشتری از صعودی‌ها بگیرد، اما بسته‌شدن ضعیف می‌گوید به جایی نمی‌رسد.

9 به زیر کندل 5 کوتاه‌مدت و تقاضای قدیمیِ کندل 3 شکستیم. اما خوردن سخت تقاضای کندل 3 یعنی باید واکنش بالاتر ببینیم.

10 این واکنشِ کندل 9 است و پول حرفه‌ای را برای حرکت نزولی اصلی ست کرده است.

11 این جالب است؛ کندل پایین‌تر از سایهٔ کندل قبلی رفت و داخل بدنهٔ کندل 3 بسته شد که هنوز معنادارترین کندلی است که باید بشکنیم.

12 بالاخره یک شکست قوی و بستن قوی. نکتهٔ اینجاست که کندل به داخل دم کندل 1 رفت. خریداران زیادی اینجا بودند و هرچند اولین باری نیست که قیمت در آن ناحیه بوده، به این ناحیه اعتبار داده می‌شود چون احتمالاً بعد از شکسته‌شدن و retest نقش مقاومت را دارد.

13 هنوز علاقه‌ای به پایین‌بردن قیمت نیست و نه صعودی‌ها و نه خرس‌ها پیشرفتی کرده‌اند. دم بسیار خفیف زیر بدنهٔ ریز یعنی صبر می‌کنیم.

14 این شروع فروش خرس‌های حرفه‌ای است. ببین سایه چطور عرضه را از کندل 12 می‌کشد و به‌صورت کندلی شبیه صعودی بسته می‌شود اما با بستن بسیار پایین روی بدنهٔ کندل 12. کتاب‌ها به تو می‌گویند این کندل اینگالف صعودی است چون کندل قبلی را در بر گرفته؛ درست، اما کتاب‌ها به تو نمی‌گویند دلیل سایه چیست و کجا رفته است.

15 چیزی که باید در این کندل نگاه کنی این است که بدنه هم نزولی است و هم داخل کندل قبلی بسته شده، اما خریدارانی بالاتر نیست چون کندل 14 آن چیزی است که صعودی محسوب می‌شود. پول حرفه‌ای بهتر می‌داند.

16 این فشار بزرگ است تا بازار به حرکت دربیاید و همهٔ کارهای قبل از این کندل در کندل 14 انجام شده و خرس‌های زیادی منتظر این حرکت بودند، در حالی که کندل 14 تریدرهای روزانه را خرید کرده بود و حالا کندل 16 آن‌ها را استاپ کرده و به سفارش‌های نزولی سوخت می‌افزاید. همچنین توجه کن کندل‌های 12، 13، 14، 15 همه روی S/R هستند.

17 چیز زیادی برای گفتن نیست؛ با سرعت خوبی در حال پایین‌رفتن هستیم و خرس‌ها دارند پول درمی‌آورند؛ جلوی این قطار باری نایست، سوارش شو.

18 خط پایین چارت من، تقاضای قدیمی است که از چارت بالایی گرفته شده. پس چرا قیمت ناگهان متوقف شد و صعودی شد؟… دو دلیل: همهٔ پول حرفه‌ای تارگت سود یکسانی ندارد و بعضی قبل از تارگت نهایی بیرون می‌آیند. این کندل سودگیری را نشان می‌دهد که خودش آخرین خرس‌هایی که در بسته‌شدن 16 وارد شدند — یعنی باز 17 — را پین کرده است. چه کسی حدس می‌زد که یک حرکت کوچک نهایی به پایین ست می‌کند. اما روی این تایم‌فریم برای خرید یک ناهار قشنگ کافی است :)

19 تقاضای قدیمی تا پیکسل پین شد و اولین نشانهٔ کندشدن بازار هم هست. دم این را به ما می‌گوید. وقتی بازار سخت می‌دود، روی یک پاره‌سکه متوقف نمی‌شود و دم‌ها و سایه‌هایی که روی سطوح قیمتی قدیمی بزرگ در تایم‌فریم‌های بالاتر می‌بینی باید توسط پول حرفه‌ای در جهت مخالف معامله شوند تا اول حرکت فعلی را متوقف کنند و حرکت بعدی را ست کنند. این هرگز تمرین ارزانی نیست و هزینهٔ زیادی دارد. ما سایه‌ها و دم‌ها را می‌بینیم و برای ورودهای خودمان دنبالشان می‌گردیم.

20. با توجه به اینکه پول حرفه‌ای به تارگتش رسیده بود، تعجبی نبود که دست‌کم یک leg کوچک به بالا ببینیم و احتمالاً retest کف تازه‌ساخته‌شده.

21 تا اینجا دیگر نزولی نیستیم و الان صعودی‌ایم، اما retest کف هنوز در دستور است مگر این‌که تست حمایت جدیدی همراه شود و این ممکن است شبیه نقطهٔ تصمیم به نظر برسد. جاهای ممکن برای یک تصمیم حساب‌شده کندل 18 و خوشهٔ 13 تا 15 هستند.

تایم‌فریم این مهم نیست چون قیمتی که در زمان رسم می‌شود فرکتالی از خودش است و نگه‌داشتن همهٔ نواحی حمایت و تقاضای قدیمی از تایم‌فریم‌های بالاتر برای استفاده روی چارت‌های تایم‌فریم پایین‌تر برای موفقیت ضروری است. مثال: معامله‌گر 1 یا 5 دقیقه‌ای که در کندل 19 فروش می‌گیرد چون شکست 18 بوده، اما نمی‌فهمد دارد به یک تایم‌فریم بالاتر بزرگِ خریداران فروش می‌زند.

بقیهٔ خطوط افقی روی چارت راهنمای جزئی برای تمرین چشمت و سمت منطقی مغزت هستند. جاهای بیشتری برای پیداکردن حمایت و مقاومت هست و می‌گذارم خودت آن‌ها را پیدا کنی.

اگر حاضری صبر کنی، قیمت همیشه جهت روشنی و لحظهٔ برگشتش را به تو نشان می‌دهد. گاهی حتی یک معامله 5min یک روز یا بیشتر طول می‌کشد تا بیاید. این چارت عمدتاً برای معامله‌گر آمریکایی است که ژست قشنگی به من کرده و من هم قدردانی‌اش را پس می‌دهم و به او می‌فهمانم ارزش بیشتری از پولِ تنها هست. بقیه برای مطالعهٔ بیشتر متریال دارند، پس از دوست آمریکایی‌مان برای ایدهٔ چارت کندل‌استیکی شماره‌گذاری‌شده تشکر کن.

آخر هفتهٔ خوبی داشته باشید همه.

Of course we wait for this to show before entering and not take them blind. Given the Euro is gaining a bullish position against the US Dollar I tend to wait for this turn to prove pro bulls are truly active.

When taking price entries off the 4hr as your lead, you are waiting for a pull back on a lower time frame back into the 4hr break. If you miss that entry, let it go. Concentrate then on lower time frame entries in the direction of the 4hr move at the end of opposing price action on lower time frames. You get a hint of the entry when price compresses and also when price action reaches exhaustion through emotional climatic movement by pro money to get you in the wrong direction, or when an area is strongly traded against once hit. Your next lower 15min chart has a nice candle with a long tail, this is buying coming in. But look how it formed? can you see what the effect that single candle had?...it filled all longs in one hit. This is only useful if the base was strong for bulls to come in and pro money being active in the market, price action even with what bulls were there does not look promising, there is no desire to push price. If you master the ability for patience and wait for tests and retests on break outs, this will save you a lot of money and make you a lot too. If the retest doesnt come and price keeps on going, just let it go and dont chase it. I got several questions on this over the past few days and when time permits I will post up a chart broken down candle by candle.

When trading during any session you have to let price come to you, and you will be waiting at historic price areas where price still has pro money waiting. All these markets traded are a logical and simplistic thing, just let it be that.

Hotochin,

Your first 60 hours will be multiplied by several years before this can click. Not everyone will 'get it'. But if you hold your patience and put in the effort, the day when this suddenly makes sense is truly a defining moment in your life. Only screen time and being disconnected from emotions will help you. Other than that the trade entries and exists are something that is determined in seconds.

I wish I could shorten your journey, but my posts here are as good as I can do for you. Learn what you can from my posts and others too, I type in my explanations of price movement with my charts and detail what I can. I said this before, and will repeat it again. My way is not THE correct, or only way to trade. It works for me and I pass along what I know for anyone to use and are welcome to tweak it in any way they wish.

There has only been one person in many years who picked up trading as a novice in six months. The guys brain was just wired right to being with whereas all others try to force a call when there is nothing to trade off of.

Your comment of getting the higher time frames marked off is a lot more significant than you give yourself credit for. The markets and their time frames we trade within are all fractals of each other. If you remove the time factor from your higher time frame analysis, the chart now could be any time frame. Therefore it is logical that your higher time frame analysis is also correct on a lower time frame. What you must do is learn to stitch them together so that the higher time frame supply/demand reactions are witnesses by you in real time on lower time frames. i.e the lower time frame will move first and you will see perhaps a 1hr and 4hr candle close with noticeable price action present. The price action can sometimes be hidden on the higher time frames and it then presents itself as a false move on the 1 and 5min charts.

I could also put it this way, there are trading methods sold online that have you trade off pin bars on the 4hr and daily. Thats all well and good, but not all 4hr and daily supply and demand areas will form pin bars and you must look at lower time frames to see what price action is doing there.

Make sense?

Keep on watching the charts and plotting your levels. If you have mastered the 4hr and daily, try the same on the 1hr. Dont move from the one hour until you nail it. Then drop down each successive time frame and mark each one at a time. The eureka moment when it comes will hit you hard and open your eyes. Give it time.

FX1,

If you are getting stopped out could it be you are still in herd mode?.....taking break outs rather than wait for price to come back to the break and then pick up left over orders where we know pro money was active?

It is all very logical if you think about this for a while. If price moves away cleanly from an area it means pro money had to have been active, the less time they spend at an area doing this tends to make for better entries on the return back to this area where the pro's know more orders 'must' be waiting to be filled. When you see a move away, do not chase it. Let price go, and then return. On a day trading chart this could take all day or more than one day, but eventually it will return. You will get filled faster on a 1 and 5 min time frame than you will on higher time frames. If you are a day trader thats what most will look for, but it is also harder to trade off the lower time frames than it is the higher time frames. Ironic that the more money you have to trade, the easier it can be:)

Price is often ramped in one direction to make it appear to day traders that this is the move of the day, and of course the media latch onto this and sell it to you. The trading books will tell you to wait for trend line/channels confirmation where you have two touches on one line and at least one touch of the other side. This is complete nonsense and could not be further from the truth as we know it. All that does is get you further from the source of the move with less profit and higher risk.

A quick example right now at 1100GMT on the S&P500 is price has been ramped up, it is now at the high price for most time frames. Who was buying here, pro's?.......you must get good value in price before you take a trade and only where it is at historic clean areas of previous movement where pro money was active, and are likely to be active again. Your target will be also very clear in your mind and set it as a hard order close while you learn.

Hope that helps a little.

What should jump out at you after marking off historic supply and demand areas is that eventually all the boxes in their respective time frames will overlap. If you wait for this to happen the probability of a winning trade is much greater.

Hotochin's comment about price getting closer is one time when this way of trading is not going to give large results, you must look for room for profit and when price gets squeezed on higher time frames pro money wont leave orders in there keeping capital tied up. Price must move between supply and demand and when any factor effects the movement over a reasonable period of time, expect a squeeze to happen and plenty chop. It is better to look for other pairs than guessing when the break will happen.

Fortunately we do have a way to deal with this, its called patience and discipline and wait for the break, then the pull back and restest of the break to see will it hold and is there excess orders waiting for a continuation. Price action at those time and at those areas is key. The old traders often mention time and price, but its meaning is lost on most traders today.

Master marking off areas and then look for price action, just get one working first and then work on the other. You are slowing getting there Hotochin, stick to it and it gets easier.

Hotochin,

Waiting for price to hit supply or demand on the monthly and weekly is not something you or I can afford. But we must be aware than when it does hit these areas there is going to be a reaction and a likely change in direction. Once the new direction has been decided by pro money, we now drop down into daily and lower time frames to look for pull backs counter to the decided direction and look for those pull backs to be the restest of the origin of the move. The retest appears deeper on lower time frames whereas the daily generally will not pull back very much.

If you think about it logically, any low time frame within a day traders pocket is ripe for false moves and stop hunts. This is how most of the larger orders get filled. When you see the price turn against a break of even a few hours, think of this as the test of the strength of the bulls or bears. If they want to continue with the move they will close some of the positions because you are now taking the orders as the market is moving. The false sense of security plays out on all low time frames and all it does is hand a very low cost and low risk entry for pro money to reverse price back on the direction of the chosen direction.

When price is between lets say the 4hr or higher time frame supply and demand, my choice is only take a trade once a pull back has come and it is into an area where pro money was active. If the move fails my risk is small. Ideally you should not take a trade when mid range between supply and demand and take the easy trades, the type you can see from across the room!

As you get more screen under your belt you will see how price wants to come back to the origin of the move. It will give you one and sometimes a second shot at getting in. There are a few gotchas in day trading and what can mess up nice entries just waiting to be taken are the release of news and the time of day. When London in particular opens and closes price will not always react as you expect if it is approaching an area of historic price action and its best to stand aside and wait for the market to settle.

It boils down to lining up time frames and historic price action with current price action. However, it takes a long time to get your brain to work against what it sees on the hard right edge of the screen. Books tell you wait for confirmation, I say active pro money is confirmation, and pro money is its own confirmation.

Doctor wrote: Hotochin,

Waiting for price to hit supply or demand on the monthly and weekly is not something you or I can afford. But we must be aware than when it does hit these areas there is going to be a reaction and a likely change in direction. Once the new direction has been decided by pro money, we now drop down into daily and lower time frames to look for pull backs counter to the decided direction and look for those pull backs to be the restest of the origin of the move. The retest appears deeper on lower time frames whereas the daily generally will not pull back very much.

If you think about it logically, any low time frame within a day traders pocket is ripe for false moves and stop hunts. This is how most of the larger orders get filled. When you see the price turn against a break of even a few hours, think of this as the test of the strength of the bulls or bears. If they want to continue with the move they will close some of the positions because you are now taking the orders as the market is moving. The false sense of security plays out on all low time frames and all it does is hand a very low cost and low risk entry for pro money to reverse price back on the direction of the chosen direction.

When price is between lets say the 4hr or higher time frame supply and demand, my choice is only take a trade once a pull back has come and it is into an area where pro money was active. If the move fails my risk is small. Ideally you should not take a trade when mid range between supply and demand and take the easy trades, the type you can see from across the room!

As you get more screen under your belt you will see how price wants to come back to the origin of the move. It will give you one and sometimes a second shot at getting in. There are a few gotchas in day trading and what can mess up nice entries just waiting to be taken are the release of news and the time of day. When London in particular opens and closes price will not always react as you expect if it is approaching an area of historic price action and its best to stand aside and wait for the market to settle.

It boils down to lining up time frames and historic price action with current price action. However, it takes a long time to get your brain to work against what it sees on the hard right edge of the screen. Books tell you wait for confirmation, I say active pro money is confirmation, and pro money is its own confirmation.

Your comment on the arrows is close. What they show is that each time pushes higher, the source of the bullish orders is checked to see will it hold, of so filter on more orders because that small pullback is enough to get many day traders stopped out. Its a low cost entry. You can stair step those entries all the way up into old supply. But of course you need the capital to do it and the patience to wait for them. My old charts show some of my scaled entries where I take up most of the origin of the move with my entry lines:)

The origin of the move was tested when price came back and sat on top of the blue box and then bolted out of there. That was classic pro money false move and load up the boat. Note the test they took and where it was. Some of those test work out to point perfection. Who would ever have thought?....there, I had to work in my old copyrighted line as I havent used it in an age.

Keep in mind that when price wants to turn at the end of the move, it will react to old areas of price action. When ever there are deeper pull backs be very wary, if price can hit one during a turn there is unlikely to be any orders worthy enough of keeping the trend in tact and the market can turn very fast and move a long way. If there are no buyers and all historic bullish orders are taken and we are at old supply on a major time frame i.e 4hr and higher, watch out below.

The price range on 1hr+ time frames makes it hard for more traders to see clearly, this is why you must mark those area right down to the 5min with a box and look for price action inside the box. The deeper price works into the box the more I get interested to trade against it especially when 4hr + is with us.

All make sense?

When you get used to trading this way, wait for the 5min to pull away from the extreme edge of the box, then come back to test the origin of that break, once that retest is done and both market timing for a major market is not near close or news to effect the pair is not due, then I will get in. Again as you progress you will find it hard to trade against the market, this is the counter intuitive part messing with your head. If it helps and lets assume you want to trade a 3 euro trade....instead put in a 1 euro trade, wait for the price to move and form another pull back which now is a retest of the previous break, now add in another 1 euro trade. Rather than take the full risk on one trade, spread your risk over a few smaller size lots. When you improve you can then determine yourself which entries you are good at and take those heavier.

Doctor wrote: Hotochin,

Waiting for price to hit supply or demand on the monthly and weekly is not something you or I can afford. But we must be aware than when it does hit these areas there is going to be a reaction and a likely change in direction. Once the new direction has been decided by pro money, we now drop down into daily and lower time frames to look for pull backs counter to the decided direction and look for those pull backs to be the restest of the origin of the move. The retest appears deeper on lower time frames whereas the daily generally will not pull back very much.

If you think about it logically, any low time frame within a day traders pocket is ripe for false moves and stop hunts. This is how most of the larger orders get filled. When you see the price turn against a break of even a few hours, think of this as the test of the strength of the bulls or bears. If they want to continue with the move they will close some of the positions because you are now taking the orders as the market is moving. The false sense of security plays out on all low time frames and all it does is hand a very low cost and low risk entry for pro money to reverse price back on the direction of the chosen direction.

When price is between lets say the 4hr or higher time frame supply and demand, my choice is only take a trade once a pull back has come and it is into an area where pro money was active. If the move fails my risk is small. Ideally you should not take a trade when mid range between supply and demand and take the easy trades, the type you can see from across the room!

As you get more screen under your belt you will see how price wants to come back to the origin of the move. It will give you one and sometimes a second shot at getting in. There are a few gotchas in day trading and what can mess up nice entries just waiting to be taken are the release of news and the time of day. When London in particular opens and closes price will not always react as you expect if it is approaching an area of historic price action and its best to stand aside and wait for the market to settle.

It boils down to lining up time frames and historic price action with current price action. However, it takes a long time to get your brain to work against what it sees on the hard right edge of the screen. Books tell you wait for confirmation, I say active pro money is confirmation, and pro money is its own confirmation.

Not compression, if price moves from one area and relatively smoothly back to the candle that formed as the effect of the move then this is a pull back. Compression is more chaotic and candle an over lap and engulf each other in a very tight manner. Picture what you want to see as a stair step up in a bullish market, and inverse on the way down. When I get time to mark up a chart I will post one to show you. The place you marked compressed is correct but it was not what I was explaining yesterday. The pull backs is where the winning trades come from, compression is where you stay out and wait.

Compression is also price being of little interest to pro money and it wanders in the direction of the last historic area where pro money was active. The explosive move later which catches most by surprise. Unless there is a rapid retest on the 5min it may not be possible to trade those moves, you have to be watching it unfold and have the boxes drawn on your chart and see price react as it touches and enters the box. One single candle can be all it takes to retest and shoot out.

Look again at your last chart with the blue box.

Price returned to the top of the box and this was a test of the origin. Remember we are looking for it to penetrate deep as we can, but any touch of the box is what we. Where you take the trade is personal preference and based on risk and capital. Redraw the box again, but this time as the prlce where it had sat on top. Now you will see price came back here too, another buy, but with fewer bullish orders remaining.

We want price to at least reach the box which is why we draw a price range with a box, any price touch of the box is good, but a deeper push tends to be better. If all we see is a touch and price reverse that signals pro money are no longer prepared to wait for price to go further before they reverse. Their reason are many and there is nothing to be gained trying to determine why they took a touch trade.

When day trading the tests of each push is glaringly obvious especially on the 1 and 5min. The 5min is probably easier for your brain to filter out the noise. I will post up a chart to show this.

Ok guys here is a chart to help explain pro money tests and what books call trend. But their idea of trend is long after the origin of the move which is why supply/demand trading creates more profit.

The bottom of the chart shows a box which is demand. Price pushes through the box, comes back to test it and moves away cleanly after. This shows pro bulls in control. If the test of this demand was something you didnt catch, you can wait until you see a less dramatic move. There are numerous white horizontal lines on the chart and these show price pushing above the last created high and these are the pull backs I refer to. These are areas where pro money will either close positions, adjust by adding more and a combination of both. Note how price tests even the break of these small areas. This happens on many time frames and when the market is moving this is one sign you must be aware of.

As previously mentioned we are not looking for pixel perfect tests, although it can be alarmingly accurate at times, we want to see these tests as shake outs of the weak hands, those wont went long on the break only to see price come back and stop them out. Part of the reason is far too many traders place stops where pro money know where to look. Books tell you place a stop below a swing or below the last bullish candle and so on. Now that you know where to look and can train your brain where stops will be and where pro money is likely to enter, you have a valuable tool by which to pull nice money from the market.

What I described is ideal for people beginning and as you gain more confidence you can look to try out scaling in and out at the beginning and end of these overall moves where a higher time frame provides the intel for the areas to draw the boxes for supply and demand.

I hope this is useful and it gels in your head and becomes second nature.

The point behind the chart is the show the principle and not pixel perfect detail. On a lower time frame you will see some pull backs even though none will be very deep or to the break of the move up. If you are thinking ahead of my chart then you are on the right track. When a lower time frame presents an opportunity you can take it as a day trader. My chart is a daily and few of us will wait around for that to unwind before getting in.

If you examine the same pair on a lower time frame and with a zoomed out view there will be many long entries there. In the past I spoke of cycles or phases and thats the wind shown there and will be represented as a fractal of other time frames. What looks like a pull back in a higher time frame is a shorting opportunity on a lower time frame once you close the position before higher time frame demand. This is counter trend but works once you know what you are doing and crystal clear about the reaction areas.

You can see how the pull backs will last up into the final push and then there is higher time reaction to be concerned about. I am out before that reaction and bag what points I can.

Hotochin,

1. I used usd/jpy only because the price action was nice and it fitted on one chart with crystal clear movement. The white horizontal lines are where more bullish entries are placed. As price pushed up in another move, it will turn back down and test the most recent push. Once this is tested, I enter long. I am satisfied to continue placing entries until I am fully committed to the amount of capital I wish to invest and the cost in risk. The target for me will be a higher time frame area. But day traders may be happy with a set point profit i.e x points or just watch it until it turns and then close out. There are a hundred ways to trade a move.

2. The only logical way to trade is once we have a new month, do you analysis on the monthly chart, then the weekly and the daily. On each new week where there is no new monthly close, work from the weekly down, then on each new day where there is no new weekly candle close, work from the daily down. You must be 100% aware of where all time frames are ALL THE TIME.

Once you have that intel you are better positioned to look for lower time frame entries.

Once a higher time frame hits historic supply or demand I wait for price to react and give me the new direction, or continuation. This is where those white lines after a reaction come in, if the trade off the first test was missed. If you want earlier entries you will need wide stops because you know from experience pro money wont give you an easy time or a simple trade. If the heat is too much, wait for a later entry where the direction is obvious and then take a pull back entry where a test is clear in your mind. How long you wait i,e the time frame is totally your decision and I cant tell you which to take. I will take any of them and if price action and tests are not very clear I can stay out or scale in. Like I say, its down to the risk you wish to take.

I hear it all the time from traders who place a trade see it go in their direction and suddenly price comes back against them, stop them out, and price reverse back in the direction of the original move. This is what I mentioned earlier with stop hunting and pro money getting cheaper prices to filter more orders in. This never changes and has been like this since the markets began. The lesson is do not take break outs, wait for a pull back and then enter once there is room for profit in the eyes of pro money, and that is a nice distance from the next supply or demand area.

3. I wouldnt call it play money, those guys make enough in a week to buy a small country. A spike on a 4hr chart is worth billions. A 24hr day is worth 4 trillion. That is not play money and they dont get it use it unless they know what they are doing. Contrary to your other comment about pro money getting efficient pricing, they have always gotten better entry prices than we do. They are the market movers, we ride on their coat tails at a more costly entry. We cannot move the market, we do not have the capital to do so. The latent flow is what happens in the pull backs I keep mentioning. It is no more exciting than left over orders that sit there wait to be filled. Some are automated orders and some are manual. The HF stuff comes in there too.

Price goes between supply and demand on ever increasing time frames, as it works it way it will go up and down as orders are filled, closed and adjusted. There is nothing secret about how it works, in fact I find it all rather boring.

3. من اسمش را پول بازی نمی‌گذارم؛ این جماعت در یک هفته آن‌قدر درمی‌آورند که یک کشور کوچک بخرند. یک اسپایک روی چارت 4 ساعته میلیاردها می‌ارزد. یک روز 24 ساعته 4 تریلیون می‌ارزد. این پول بازی نیست و آن را به دست نمی‌آورند و خرج نمی‌کنند مگر بدانند چه می‌کنند. برخلاف آن حرف دیگرت درباره اینکه پول حرفه‌ای قیمت‌گذاری کارآمد می‌گیرد، آن‌ها همیشه قیمت ورود بهتری از ما گرفته‌اند. آن‌ها بازار را حرکت می‌دهند و ما با ورود گران‌تر، از دم‌شان آویزان می‌شویم. ما نمی‌توانیم بازار را حرکت بدهیم، سرمایه‌اش را نداریم. جریان نهفته همان چیزی است که در پولبک‌هایی که مدام از آن حرف می‌زنم رخ می‌دهد. هیچ هیجان بیشتری از سفارش‌های باقی‌مانده‌ای که آنجا نشسته‌اند و منتظر پر شدن‌اند ندارد. بعضی سفارش‌ها خودکارند و بعضی دستی. چیزهای فرکانس بالا هم آنجا سر و کله‌شان پیدا می‌شود.

قیمت بین عرضه و تقاضا در تایم‌فریم‌های هرچه بزرگ‌تر حرکت می‌کند؛ همان‌طور که راهش را می‌رود، بالا و پایین می‌رود چون سفارش‌ها پر، بسته و تنظیم می‌شوند. در اینکه چطور کار می‌کند هیچ رازی نیست؛ در واقع من همه‌اش را نسبتاً خسته‌کننده می‌دانم.

Taking a zoomed out view on the weekly there should be obvious room for profit on this chart. The higher time frames give more guidance than day traders tend to give credit, the attitude is, it takes so long for them to close that opportunities are missed. Whats really missing is the benefit from the obvious and easiest route to a target and where it is clear to see. If you take the same pair and drop down one time frame at a time and see where this move began. Do you see anything interesting in the price action in the very recent past i.e last few days?

Now look at historic bottoms to the left, note the deep spikes into price, this is removing pro bull orders and if the same thing has been done a number of times in the past, how much additional orders do you think are left?......likely little or none. Books tells you the more an area is tested it will form strong support. Sorry book authors, but that is complete tripe and as far from the truth as it gets. The more an area is tested the weaker it becomes in the direction of the original move away, bullish in this instance.

Perhaps I should write a new trading book. Opinions for titles?......The day trader and the manure from media and Wall st......nah too long.

Lower in the chart I placed an S/R line. This is an obvious target and the single spike down will be a nice reaction area when price gets close to it. I do not have a crystal ball and cannot say how this will play out, all I know is that we will eventually get down there and from this time frame I want to see the most logical and obvious place for profit. Would you buy where we are right now?.....look at the historic highs, all preceding highs are getting lower and no clear desire to go higher.

Given the fundamentals for the Australian economy and their banks dependance on over seas funding it is likely their economy will shrink and a taste of doom and gloom set in. This is already been shown in export figures and the Gov wish to now make closer ties with Asia for free trade etc. Sure it has been talked about for a long time, but when you can no longer hide behind or massage the numbers (not hinting any gov would ever do this of course) it is then time you need to do what should have been done long ago. China is a major importer of Australian raw materials and they too will continue to drop off now. What has this got to do with us trading currencies?.........There are three monthly candles per quarter, and gov figures come out each quarter. To see the bigger picture be aware of what the numbers are and what they tell. Compare the gov story to the forex market and see which is giving you both direction and room for profit and then look to lower time frames for entry based on price action.

The precursor to a market fall is bad news. Even if the market was setting up on a higher time frame to fall, pro money like to hide their intentions for a time prior to this by ramping price. This gets you in and helps then filter out some of the long held positions, and as momentum takes over then buy take the positions you now place so they now trade against you. As time marches onward I expect to hear more bad news about Australia and the currency move lower.

The two orange lines outline a range where price has been contained for the past day or so. The S and R on these lines represent what price is likely to do when either is broken. After price reached supply it will sell off which it done at your FTR. It fell to the bottom of the range where it found both support and demand, although lesser demand than previous visits. S و R روی این خطوط نشان می‌دهند قیمت وقتی هرکدام بشکند احتمالاً چه می‌کند. همهٔ این حمایت و مقاومت کلاسیک است و چیزی پیچیده‌تر از همین نیست. وقتی قیمت داخل رنج سوار است، بالای رنج نقش مقاومت و پایین رنج نقش حمایت را دارد، تا وقتی شکسته شوند.

اولین باکس آبی شکست رنج است، اما به سمت عرضهٔ نزدیک چپ چارت. هیچ بستن بالای معناداری نداشتیم. وقتی قیمت از اینجا دور افتاد به FTR تو می‌رود. به روش نسبتاً سادهٔ معامله من، این قیمت برگشتن به مبدأ حرکت و رفتن به عرضه‌ای است که فشار قبلی به بالا ساخته چون هنوز رنج‌معامله است و تو در بالای رنج‌ها می‌فروشی و در پایینشان می‌خری… اگر واقعاً حریص باشی و اعصاب فولادی داشته باشی.

بعد از اینکه قیمت به عرضه رسید، آن را فروخت که در FTR تو انجام شد. به پایین رنج افتاد که هم حمایت و هم تقاضا پیدا کرد، هرچند تقاضای کمتری نسبت به بازدیدهای قبلی. بخش خطرناک به نظرم در گرفتن تریدی از این جفت امروز، موقعیت قیمت در تایم‌فریم‌های بالاتر است. خیلی نزدیک به یک سطح تقاضای بزرگ است و همچنین سوئینگ‌های تنگ‌تری بین سطوح روزانه و هفتگی می‌سازد و قیمت می‌تواند از جایی که هست بیفتد. spike جالبی روی روزانه برای 4 مارس هست. همچنین در 2 مه درست قبل از 11:45 روی چارت من می‌توانی تست کف‌ها را ببینی؛ این پول حرفه‌ای بود که برای سفارش‌های بیشتر می‌رفت و معامله را برای حرکت صعودی بسته. price action امروز حتی به داخل آن کندل برگشت تا ببیند سفارش‌های بیشتری مانده یا نه. کندل ظهر بقیهٔ داستان را می‌گوید با هیچ شانسی برای ورود بعد از آن.

baltimore, a post for you and also for another member who asked some weeks ago for a candle by candle break down as I have done in the past.

For long term trades the news is of little interest to me unless I am about to get in or out of a trade. i time my entries away from news releases in case the reaction to the news pushes price away from my entry price. Overall the news tends to accelerate where price was going.

I am going to break down some analysis on soybeans from the weekly down to the 4hr chart. The same principles apply to all financial instruments and the only difference you get with non forex instruments is the open and close prices which are not as orderly.

Here is the zoomed out 10 mile view of the weekly soybean chart. The lower two green lines outline a trading range where spent considerable time. The upper two orange(?) lines also show a less than perfect trading range where price has spent considerable time. Looking on this time frame is is clear we have come from a high price and sold off and developed a trading range. The first question that comes to mind is, where is there room for profit and in which direction. To answer the direction part of the question we can see we came from a high price and because markets cycle between high and lo, we now want to look for where is there an obvious place for price to go, if we accept that price is indeed going to continue its ride down.

What would be a sign of price not willing to get back to test old highs/old supply/historic sell orders?....how about the effect of the current closed weekly candle. We see it punched through the top of the trading range, but closed inside it. If nothing else, would it be fair to say that price is likely to test the bottom of the trading range?....you have to answer this for yourself and engage the logical side of your brain, not the emotional side.

If I accepted it will go lower, do I have room for profit?......yes, I have plenty room. Can I be sure it will go lower, no. But are there other factors to help me, well, how about the overall price of the closed candle, would it cost much for pro money to push it back up, and if so, how far will it have to go before they see an obvious target and not destroy a potential larger shorting profit target. Clearly they could go back and test the overall high back in September of 2012. Given this is a commodity, prices rise on bad news. If we get poor crop yields price will rise. At the moment it is too early to tell. For the moment we reserve our judgement and plan around what we see, not what we think. Thinking make you poor whereas waiting makes your account grow.

Now we move to a closer look and review the daily time frame.

Again the orange lines show the trading range I mentioned and as you all know by know a trading range is established support and resistance, which is also supply and demand, which is also buyers and sellers, or bulls and bears, depending on which suits you. Price has on two occasions spiked through the top of the trading range and close lower. This is a false break, stop hunt and pro money testing to see if orders remain above current price (at the time). The trading range has a potential 1400 points approximately and plenty room for profit within it. Clearly it has well defined areas where we can buy and sell. Within the last bullish move up the top of the range there was an area of interest developed. Like all ranges we can never know where and when they will break and continue in the chosen direction. As each retest of the edges of the range are tested pro money has a costly choice and either the pro bulls or pro bears will cause the range to break. When we see areas of interest develop within the range we must pay attention when price comes back to them.

The same daily chart is up this time and zoomed in a little to get clearer data. The orange lines are the established edges of the trading range and a few points I wanted to show are marked. Note the large bullish candle, this was a bullish break in comparison to the supply to the left where there was a lot of sellers willing to get involved. This new green candle was a sign price wants to go higher. There was no follow through and a gap down happened on the next candle. i will come back to this green candle shortly. Now look at the large bullish candle that broke the overall range in grand style. unfortunately it broke and more importantly closed back inside the range. This was a false break getting the herd long, which was cheap short orders for pro bears. It was also a stop hunt when the herd who were long same price come right back to them and get stopped out, and when you are stopped out it means someone else has had to take your sell order....and you got it, pro bears take your money again and all on the same candle. Who ever would have guessed such tricks like this happen daily and the herd fall for it all the time. I define 'time' as the time the financial markets have been in operation. I know what you are saying to yourself, how could the herd be so silly. That my friend is where the emotional side of your brain comes into play.....the market is moving and I better get in fast or I will miss it. Wrong!....do no chase the market, let it come to your price and then jump in. This will be counter intuitive until you grapple with your emotions.

Looking again at the long wick on the second last candle it will become apparent the closing price was no different to the previous candle. Logic tells you, there is no bullish move and it was nothing more than a low cost way for pro money to send price back down. Proof came in the next candle, a bearish engulfing candle which closed slightly below the bullish candle to its left. Thats enough for the bias to become bearish and await a retrace for an entry, or pull the trigger as it stands and put up with the draw down. One item to look for which most traders will be blind to, is the large green candle where I marked it as being able to drive prices lower. It will do this due to the fact that anyone who went long in that candle will close out as price approaches again. They will seek a free trade close if possible, this then will drive price back up into the origin of the bearish break and then becomes the perfect launching point for bears to load up. Of course, we have to wait for father time to tick by and tell us if this analysis is correct and only trade off closed candles with history to back it up.

Here is a 4hr chart and once again the orange lines are still holding well for an overall trading range. Within the range I have marked up the 1st reaction area which as you can see here was hit nicely. On the top of the range was the false break and subsequent close which is very dramatic and hard lesson to the herd. This lesson will be forgotten about in a few days and people will still react to breaks like this forever more. Greed is a wonderful thing to profit against.

There is about 500 point of profit shorting from where price is now down to the top of the box. It is not for me to tell you how or when to trade. I am showing you money in motion and where it can go. You decide where you want to take it.

As price went from the bottom of the range to the top you can see test after test taking in all the bullish orders and was a text book example of how markets used look in the good old days before the financial shake out. If price has taken pro money long as it went up to their obvious target, does it not seem reasonable that on the way back down there will be little interest from pro bulls to buy again?.....probably not. This then suggests that any move down will happen faster than the move up and if such a move happened, could it build enough momentum from the herd to get price down through the bottom of the trading range?....yes very possible given the willingness of the herd to jump into a fast moving market, they do like to show they are risk takers even if they dont admit it.

One final point on this chart is the lower part of the box. Note price action to its left where I marked it for interest on the way down. If we see momentum from the herd, pro bears are also there by the boat load from historic price action and as yet, they have not had price come to reach them. These people have the sense to wait for price whereas the herd will keep chasing it and in all the wrong places.

Finally another daily chart and it is zoomed in and a candle by candle break down.

It is important to know where we are on the big picture and this is shown by the orange lines and helps contain our brain in the correct place.

1, A bullish false break of an out of pic bearish candle. This was the classic means by which to get a low cost short entry for pro bears.

2. React to candle 1. Note the gap open lower and perfect test of candle 1's low. On a lower time frame there was likely the perfect short entry.

3. Long body and strong move into support, this is similar to how false breaks work as it gives the impression price will move much further due to the apparent strength of the candle. Anytime you see strong candles close into major supply/demand support/resistance areas, watch out and keep stops close. Most pro money are gunning for a target and wont give you much time to close out, but plenty time to let your emotions rule your logical brain with....I need to get in on this.

4. Warning sign, if the previous candle was so powerful how come it didnt follow through. Thats the herd mentality and very clear from this candle the target was reach and its time to load up long by soaking up the short herd.

5. A nice test of candle 3 open and absorbing the last of the herd shorts. The close above candle 4 is a clear indication of no more bears remain. Price can now setup a small trading range or head back up into supply/resistance.

6. Another clear sign of no interest in the down side and a very tight price between open and close.

7. On a lower time frame this would have been seen as a false bearish break designed for the herd. However the candle is not engulfing enough historic price action to be taken as actual intent. If pro money were behind it, what would they have been selling off?.....there is not enough orders to get enough money into the market.

8. An engulf of the previous candle and the herd just got the sucker punch again. Will they ever learn.

9. The wick on this candle is search ever higher for liquidity. Its wick helped pull in the last remaining shorts in the herd and closed above all the area where pro bulls were absorbing shorts.

10. The power of pro bulls now obvious to everyone and closed above candle 2 open which was the origin of the bearish move.

11. An inside bar which is still bullish, there is no close below the previous candle but enough to get some of the herd short again.

12. As this candle was forming we would have seen the herd short again on the basis of candle 11 looking like a sell off. But as we know it only makes sense to trade off closed candle and from where there is an active market in our chosen direction. There cannot have been pro bears in that candle because all are closed out long by now.

13 & 14. These candle are tests of the pro bullish money in candle 12 and of 11. The tails penetrate into the body of 12 and into the open of 11. Price reacts to more than just the previous candle, it has to test other areas further back to see will a move hold and if there are more orders remaining.

15. First of the bullish move that everyone can see being clear of all the other candle to the left. It is now too late for a trade because it less profit and higher risk given we are getting much closer to candle 1 which was the cause of so much pain.

16 + 17 + 18. All very strong candle with very little retrace showing pro money is keen for a target to be hit. It is also setting up as a parabolic move which never ends happily if you chase it.

19. now we break candle 1 and the herd are over joyed and jump in long because they see swing high being broken and this is a strong sign.....so they read in their expensive trading books.

20. This candle is the confirmation the herd wanted and that they knew they were right all along and throw everything they have it at because it will never stop going up and they will be a millionaire in a few hours time and how they cracked the secret code of the market.

21. Oh dear, the herd just got toasted and they lost their shirt once again, stops all pulled out and left wondering how they were so wrong. All the while paying little attention to the fact that pro money had set them up to help push price into supply/resistance/pro bears and the outcome then is a foregone conclusion.

The main thing to get from this post is that there is a story in every candle once you take it in context with higher time frames and with the candle previous to the current one. These same principles apply equally to all time frames with the only difference in low time frames is the noise introduced by many more false moves and high frequency trading.

Taking a trade must be done with a clear view of where there is room for profit and in the direction chosen by pro money in an active market. I hold the view that the average day trader is not willing to wait for at least the 4hr chart to line up with major areas of interest and then the day trader is putting him/herself at a distinct disadvantage. if you find you only can afford to trade the 1 or 5 min chart, do the right thing and only take entries in the overall direction of the market as pull backs develop. The spiky nature of those time frames will cost you winning trades and you will have to find some mechanism to deal with that.

I hope this is of benefit to you.

baltimore، پستی برای تو و برای یک عضو دیگر که چند هفته پیش هم مانند گذشته شکست کندل‌به‌کندل را خواسته بود.

برای معاملات بلندمدت، اخبار برای من جذابیت کمی دارند مگر اینکه بخواهم وارد یا خارج شوم. ورودهایم را طوری می‌گذارم که با انتشار اخبار تداخل نداشته باشد، در صورت اینکه واکنش به خبر قیمت را از قیمت ورودم دور کند. در مجموع اخبار تمایل دارند جایی که قیمت می‌رفت را تندتر کنند.

می‌خواهم چند تحلیل روی سویا را از هفتگی تا نمودار 4 ساعته بشکافم. همین اصول برای همهٔ ابزارهای مالی صدق می‌کند و تنها تفاوت ابزارهای غیر فارکس، قیمت‌های باز و بسته‌شدن است که آن‌قدر منظم نیستند.

این دید بزرگنمایی‌شدهٔ از دور برای نمودار هفتگی سویا است. دو خط سبز پایین یک رنج معاملاتی را مشخص می‌کنند که زمان قابل‌توجهی در آن گذرانده شده. دو خط نارنجی(؟) بالایی هم یک رنج معاملاتیِ کمتر از کامل را نشان می‌دهند که قیمت زمان زیادی در آن بوده. با نگاه به این تایم‌فریم روشن است که از یک قیمت بالا آمده‌ایم، سقوط کرده و یک رنج معاملاتی ساخته شده. اولین سؤالی که به ذهن می‌رسد این است: کجا جای سود هست و در چه جهتی؟ برای پاسخ به بخش جهت، می‌بینیم از قیمت بالا آمده‌ایم و چون بازارها بین بالا و پایین چرخه می‌زنند، حالا باید دنبال جایی باشیم که قیمت مسیر روشنی برای رفتن به آن داشته باشد، اگر بپذیریم که قیمت واقعاً قرار است سیر نزولی‌اش را ادامه دهد.

چه نشانه‌ای می‌گوید قیمت مایل نیست برگردد و سقف‌های قدیمی/عرضهٔ قدیمی/سفارش‌های فروش تاریخی را تست کند؟… چطور دربارهٔ اثر کندل هفتگیِ بسته‌شدهٔ فعلی؟ می‌بینیم که بالای رنج معاملاتی را سوراخ کرده، اما داخل آن بسته شده. اگر چیز دیگری نباشد، منصفانه است بگوییم قیمت احتمالاً کف رنج را تست می‌کند؟… خودت باید به این سؤال جواب بدهی و بخش منطقی ذهنت را به کار بگیری، نه بخش احساسی را.

اگر بپذیرم که پایین‌تر می‌رود، جای سود دارم؟… بله، جای سود فراوان است. می‌توانم مطمئن باشم که پایین می‌رود؟ نه. اما آیا عوامل دیگری برای کمک هست؟ خب، چه فکر می‌کنی دربارهٔ قیمت کلی کندل بسته‌شده؛ برای پول حرفه‌ای هزینهٔ زیادی دارد که آن را دوباره بالا ببرد؟ و اگر بزند، تا کجا باید برود تا یک تارگت واضح ببیند و تارگت سود شورتِ بزرگ‌ترِ بالقوه را نابود نکند؟ واضح است که می‌توانند برگردند و سقف کلیِ September 2012 را تست کنند. چون این یک کالای اولیه است، قیمت‌ها با خبر بد بالا می‌روند. اگر عملکرد محصول کشاورزی ضعیف شود قیمت بالا می‌رود. فعلاً زود است برای قضاوت. فعلاً قضاوت را به تعویق می‌اندازیم و حول آنچه می‌بینیم برنامه می‌ریزیم، نه آنچه فکر می‌کنیم. فکر کردن فقیر می‌کند، صبر کردن حساب را رشد می‌دهد.

حالا سراغ نگاه نزدیک‌تر و مرور تایم‌فریم روزانه می‌رویم.

دوباره خطوط نارنجی همان رنج معاملاتی است که گفتم و همان‌طور که همه می‌دانید، رنج معاملاتی همان حمایت و مقاومتِ تثبیت‌شده است که همان عرضه و تقاضا است و همان خریدار و فروشنده یا صعودی و خرس، بسته به اینکه کدام برایت خوش‌تر است. قیمت دو بار از بالای رنج معاملاتی جهش کرده و پایین بسته شده. این یک شکست کاذب، شکار حد ضرر و تست پول حرفه‌ای است برای اینکه ببینند آیا سفارشی بالای قیمت فعلی (در آن زمان) باقی مانده است یا نه. رنج معاملاتی حدود 1400 پوینت پتانسیل دارد و جای سود فراوانی داخلش هست. واضح است نواحی مشخصی برای خرید و فروش دارد. در آخرین حرکت صعودی به بالای رنج، ناحیه‌ای از علاقه ایجاد شد. مثل همهٔ رنج‌ها، هرگز نمی‌توانیم بدانیم کجا و کی می‌شکنند و در جهت انتخاب‌شده ادامه می‌دهند. با هر تست مجدد لبه‌های رنج، پول حرفه‌ای انتخابی پرهزینه دارد و یا صعودی‌های حرفه‌ای یا خرس‌های حرفه‌ای رنج را می‌شکنند. وقتی نواحی علاقه را داخل رنج می‌بینیم که شکل می‌گیرند، باید وقتی قیمت به آن‌ها برمی‌گردد توجه کنیم.

این بار همان نمودار روزانه با زوم بیشتر برای دادهٔ واضح‌تر است. خطوط نارنجی لبه‌های تثبیت‌شدهٔ رنج معاملاتی‌اند و چند نکته‌ای که می‌خواستم نشان بدهم علامت‌گذاری شده‌اند. به کندل صعودی بزرگ توجه کن؛ این نسبت به عرضهٔ سمت چپ که فروشندگان زیادی آمادهٔ درگیر شدن بودند، یک شکست صعودی بود. این کندل سبز جدید نشانه‌ای بود که قیمت می‌خواهد بالاتر برود. ادامه‌ای نیامد و در کندل بعدی یک گپ به پایین رخ داد. به‌زودی به این کندل سبز برمی‌گردم. حالا به کندل صعودی بزرگی نگاه کن که کل رنج را با شکوه شکست. متأسفانه شکست و مهم‌تر از آن، داخل رنج بسته شد. این یک شکست کاذب بود که توده را خرید کرد و سفارش‌های فروش ارزان برای خرس‌های حرفه‌ای ساخت. همزمان، یک شکار حد ضرر بود؛ توده‌ای که همان قیمت خرید شده بود دقیقاً برمی‌گشت و استاپ می‌خورد، و وقتی استاپ می‌خوری یعنی کس دیگری مجبور شده سفارش فروش تو را بگیرد… و حدس زدی، خرس‌های حرفه‌ای دوباره پول تو را می‌گیرند و همه در همان یک کندل. چه کسی فکرش را می‌کرد چنین ترفندهایی روزانه اتفاق می‌افتد و توده همه‌وقت به آن می‌افتد. 'زمان' را به‌عنوان زمانی تعریف می‌کنم که بازارهای مالی فعال بوده‌اند. می‌دانم چه می‌گویی در ذهنت، چطور توده می‌تواند این‌قدر احمق باشد. رفیق، همان‌جاست که بخش احساسی ذهنت وارد بازی می‌شود… بازار دارد حرکت می‌کند و بهتر است سریع وارد شوم وگرنه می‌سوزم. اشتباه!… بازار را تعقیب نکن، بگذار به قیمتت بیاید و بعد بپر. این تا وقتی با احساساتت دست‌وپنجه نرم کنی، خلاف شهودت خواهد بود.

با نگاه دوباره به فیتیلهٔ بلند کندل یکی‌مانده به آخر، روشن می‌شود قیمت بسته‌شدن با کندل قبلی فرقی نداشت. منطق به تو می‌گوید حرکت صعودی وجود نداشته و این چیزی جز راه کم‌هزینه‌ای برای پول حرفه‌ای نبود تا قیمت را دوباره پایین بفرستد. اثبات در کندل بعدی آمد: یک کندل اینگالف نزولی که کمی زیر کندل صعودیِ سمت چپش بسته شد. برای اینکه جهت‌گیری نزولی شود و منتظر پولبک برای ورود بمانی، یا همین حالا ماشه را بکشی و ریسکِ دراودان را بپذیری، همین کافی است. یک مورد که بیشتر معامله‌گران کورش هستند، همان کندل سبز بزرگی است که آن را علامت زدم به‌عنوان چیزی که می‌تواند قیمت را پایین بیاورد. این کار را می‌کند چون هرکس در آن کندل خرید شده باشد، وقتی قیمت دوباره نزدیک می‌شود پوزیشنش را می‌بندد. اگر ممکن باشد دنبال بستن رایگان می‌روند که این خودش قیمت را به مبدأ شکست نزولی برمی‌گرداند و آنجا نقطهٔ پرتاب کاملی برای خرس‌هاست تا پوزیشن بسازند. البته باید صبر کنیم پدر زمان بگذرد و بگوید این تحلیل درست است یا نه و فقط روی کندل‌های بسته‌شده معامله کنیم که تاریخچهٔ پشتیبانشان را دارد.

این هم یک نمودار 4 ساعته و دوباره خطوط نارنجی برای یک رنج معاملاتی کلی هنوز خوب نگه داشته‌اند. داخل رنج ناحیهٔ واکنش اول را علامت زدم که همان‌طور که اینجا می‌بینی خوب به آن رسید. بالای رنج همان شکست کاذب و بسته‌شدن متعاقبش بود که درسی بسیار دراماتیک و سخت برای توده است. این درس چند روز دیگر فراموش می‌شود و آدم‌ها همیشه به چنین شکست‌هایی واکنش نشان می‌دهند. طمع چیزی شگفت‌انگیز است که از آن سود می‌گیری.

از جایی که قیمت الان است تا بالای باکس حدود 500 پوینت سود برای فروش هست. به من نیست که بگویم چطور یا کی معامله کنی. من دارم پولِ در حرکت و اینکه کجا می‌تواند برود را به تو نشان می‌دهم. تو تصمیم می‌گیری کجا می‌خواهی بگیری‌اش.

وقتی قیمت از کف رنج به بالا رفت، تست بعد از تست را می‌بینی که همهٔ سفارش‌های صعودی را می‌گرفت و مثال کتاب درسی بود از شکل بازارها در روزهای خوب قدیمی قبل از تکان مالی. اگر قیمت پول حرفه‌ای را در رفتن به بالا خرید کرده و به تارگت آشکارشان رسیده، آیا منطقی به نظر نمی‌رسد که در راه برگشت به پایین، تمایل کمی از خرس‌های حرفه‌ای برای خریدن دوباره باشد؟… احتمالاً نه. پس این نشان می‌دهد هر حرکت به پایین سریع‌تر از حرکت به بالا خواهد بود و اگر چنین حرکتی رخ دهد، می‌تواند مومنتوم کافی از توده بسازد تا قیمت از کف رنج معاملاتی پایین برود؟… بله، بسیار ممکن است با توجه به تمایل توده به پریدن در بازار سریع‌حرکت؛ دوست دارند نشان دهند ریسک‌پذیرند حتی اگر اعتراف نکنند.

یک نکتهٔ پایانی دربارهٔ این نمودار، بخش پایین باکس است. به price action سمت چپش توجه کن که برای علاقه در مسیر نزول علامت زده‌ام. اگر مومنتوم از توده ببینیم، خرس‌های حرفه‌ای هم به‌وفور از price action تاریخی آنجا هستند و تا حالا قیمت را به آن‌ها نرسانده‌اند. این آدم‌ها عقل دارند منتظر قیمت بمانند، در حالی که توده مدام تعقیبش می‌کند و همیشه در جاهای اشتباه.

در آخر، یک نمودار روزانهٔ دیگر که زوم شده و شکست کندل‌به‌کندل دارد.

مهم است که در تصویر بزرگ کجا هستیم و این با خطوط نارنجی نشان داده شده و به محتوای مغزمان در جای درست کمک می‌کند.

1، یک شکست صعودی کاذب روی کندل نزولیِ بیرون از تصویر. این راه کلاسیک بود تا ورود فروش کم‌هزینه‌ای برای خرس‌های حرفه‌ای بگیرند.

2. واکنش به کندل 1. به گپ باز شدن پایین‌تر و تست بی‌نقص کف کندل 1 توجه کن. روی تایم‌فریم پایین‌تر احتمالاً ورود فروش بی‌نقصی بوده.

3. بدنهٔ بلند و حرکت قوی به داخل حمایت؛ این شبیه نحوهٔ کار شکست‌های کاذب است چون این تصور را می‌دهد که قیمت خیلی بیشتر حرکت می‌کند، به‌خاطر قدرت ظاهری کندل. هر وقت کندل‌های قوی را دیدی که داخل نواحی عرضه/تقاضا، حمایت/مقاومت بزرگ بسته می‌شوند، مراقب باش و استاپ‌ها را نزدیک نگه دار. بیشتر پول حرفه‌ای دنبال تارگت است و به تو وقت زیادی برای بستن نمی‌دهد، اما وقت زیادی می‌دهد که احساساتت روی مغز منطقی‌ات حاکم شود با… باید وارد این شوم.

4. نشانهٔ هشدار: اگر کندل قبلی این‌قدر قدرتمند بود، چرا ادامه نداد؟ آن روحیهٔ توده است و از این کندل کاملاً مشخص است که تارگت رسیده و وقتش است که با جمع کردن فروش‌های توده، پوزیشن خرید بگیری.

5. تست خوبِ باز شدن کندل 3 و جذب آخرین فروش‌های توده. بسته شدن بالای کندل 4 نشانهٔ روشنی است که دیگر خرسی نمانده. قیمت حالا می‌تواند یک رنج معاملاتی کوچک بسازد یا به داخل عرضه/مقاومت برگردد.

6. نشانهٔ روشن دیگرِ بی‌علاقگی به سمت پایین و قیمت بسیار تنگ بین باز و بسته.

7. روی تایم‌فریم پایین‌تر، این به‌عنوان یک شکست نزولی کاذبِ طراحی‌شده برای توده دیده می‌شد. اما کندل آن‌قدر price action تاریخی را اینگالف نکرده که قصد واقعی تلقی شود. اگر پول حرفه‌ای پشتش بود، چه چیزی می‌خواست بفروشد؟… سفارش کافی برای اینکه پول کافی وارد بازار شود نیست.

8. اینگالفِ کندل قبلی و توده دوباره یک مشتِ غافلگیرکننده خورد. آیا هیچ‌وقت یاد می‌گیرند؟

9. فیتیلهٔ این کندل به‌دنبال نقدینگیِ هرچه بالاتر است. فیتیله‌اش به کشیدن آخرین فروش‌های باقی‌ماندهٔ توده کمک کرد و بالای کل ناحیه‌ای که صعودی‌های حرفه‌ای در آن فروش‌ها را جذب می‌کردند بسته شد.

10. قدرت صعودی‌های حرفه‌ای حالا برای همه آشکار است و بالای باز شدن کندل 2 بسته شد که مبدأ حرکت نزولی بود.

11. یک داخل‌باری که هنوز صعودی است؛ بسته شدن زیر کندل قبلی نیست، اما برای اینکه بخشی از توده دوباره فروش شوند کافی است.

12. در حالی که این کندل در حال شکل‌گیری بود، توده را دوباره فروش می‌دیدیم چون کندل 11 شبیه فروش به نظر می‌رسید. اما همان‌طور که می‌دانیم، فقط روی کندل بسته‌شده معامله کردن معنا دارد و از جایی که بازار فعال در جهت انتخابی ما هست. نمی‌توانسته خرس حرفه‌ای در آن کندل باشد چون همه تا آن موقع خرید خود را بسته‌اند.

13 و 14. این کندل‌ها تست پول حرفه‌ای صعودی در کندل 12 و 11 هستند. فیتیله‌ها به داخل بدنهٔ 12 و به داخل باز شدن 11 نفوذ می‌کنند. قیمت به بیشتر از فقط کندل قبلی واکنش نشان می‌دهد؛ باید نواحی دیگری که دورترند را تست کند تا ببیند آیا حرکتی دوام می‌آورد و آیا سفارش‌های بیشتری باقی مانده است یا نه.

15. اولین کندلِ حرکت صعودی که همه می‌توانند ببینند، از همهٔ کندل‌های سمت چپش جداست. حالا برای معامله دیر است چون سود کمتر و ریسک بیشتر است با توجه به اینکه به کندل 1 که علت آن‌همه درد بود خیلی نزدیک شده‌ایم.

16 + 17 + 18. همه کندل‌های بسیار قوی با پولبک بسیار کم که نشان می‌دهد پول حرفه‌ای مشتاق است تارگت زده شود. همچنین دارد به‌عنوان یک حرکت سهمی شکل می‌گیرد که اگر تعقیبش کنی هیچ‌وقت خوشی ندارد.
